candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos III.55
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.55 (c. 350 AD)

'For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps' — Athanasius marks Christos epathen hyper hymōn (Christ suffered for us) as the SOTERIOLOGICAL-PARADIGMATIC pair: the suffering is BOTH substitutionary (hyper hymōn — on-your-behalf, in-your-place) AND paradigmatic (hypogrammon — a writing-pattern-to-copy). Christ's-suffering simultaneously redeems and exemplifies; the soteriological efficacy makes the moral-imitation possible rather than mere-moralism. The Word qua-divine cannot suffer; the Word qua-assumed-flesh genuinely-suffers and the suffering is salvifically-imputed to the Word's-Person. Pairs with 1 Pet 3:18 (Christ once-suffered for sins) as the canonical-substitutionary-Petrine-pair.
